name: order-gated greedy acceptance: a candidate is rejected before evaluation unless it is smaller under the order, and adopted only if it satisfies the predicate, is smaller, and the transition is allowed

provenance.ancestor: hypothesis Shrinker.cached_test_function + incorporate_test_data; the same shape in shrinking.common.Shrinker.consider

sources.ref: hypothesis 6.165.10 (Techne lock; shrinker.py sha256 f364cbff...) hypothesis/internal/conjecture/shrinker.py 397-427 (cached_test_function: prefix check; sort_key(self.nodes) < sort_key(nodes) -> reject; choice_permitted gate; engine call; incorporate_test_data; check_calls), 429-441 (incorporate_test_data: status >= VALID, predicate, sort_key smaller, allow_transition)

hypothesis 6.165.10 (Techne lock; shrinker.py sha256 f364cbff...) hypothesis/internal/conjecture/shrinking/common.py 92-120 (consider: make_immutable, canonical dedupe against a seen set, check_invariants, left_is_better, predicate, accept)

questions.ancestry: Both copies are in the pinned bytes; the two files were read separately and the shape matched. Whether one was derived from the other is unknown (T2 at best); the boundary was drawn from the repeated flow, not from either def.
questions.mechanism: Given the current best and a candidate: (1) if the candidate is not strictly smaller under the order, do not even evaluate it; (2) if it violates a constraint (or was seen before, in the standalone form), do not evaluate it; (3) evaluate; (4) adopt iff the property holds and (in the engine form) an external allow_transition agrees. Every adoption is a strict decrease under the order, so the process cannot cycle.
questions.input: current best (a choice sequence or a plain value), a candidate of the same kind, a predicate, a strict total-ish order (c02 or a left_is_better)
questions.output: a Bool (adopted or not) and, as a side effect, the new best
questions.state: the current best; in the standalone form a seen-set of canonical values (so a rejected candidate is never re-evaluated); in the engine form the evaluation count and the stall counter (check_calls raises StopShrinking)
questions.assumptions: that the order is strict and well-founded on the values that arise (termination follows); that the predicate is deterministic (the engine form exits FLAKY otherwise, c17); that 'smaller before evaluating' loses nothing worth having -- i.e. no larger intermediate is ever needed to reach a smaller final (the greedy assumption)
questions.interface: consider(candidate) -> bool over (best, predicate, order); the engine form adds allow_transition(best, candidate) -> bool and a call counter
questions.fitness_value: unknown -- claimed: monotone descent under the order with no wasted evaluations on non-improvements; the fraction of proposed candidates rejected before evaluation is the natural measure and was not measured (the specimen's profiling report counts calls per pass, not pre-evaluation rejections).
questions.failure_landscape: (a) greedy: a local minimum under the pass set is a fixed point (the specimen's docstring says so: 'a local minimum for each shrink pass'); (b) the order decides everything -- a candidate that is simpler by the CONSUMER's order but not by c02 is rejected at step (1) unseen (Proteus states exactly this: 'THAT IS NOT THIS ORDER'); (c) allow_transition is a hook whose semantics live outside.
questions.ablation: unknown -- designed: remove step (1) (evaluate everything, adopt only if smaller). Prediction: identical results, more evaluations. Not run; needs a patched copy, not a switch.
questions.decomposability: (1) the pre-evaluation order gate, (2) the validity/seen gate, (3) the accept rule. (1) and (3) share the order; (2) is c15/scaffolding. Nothing further.
questions.composability: Any local search over a totally ordered space with a Boolean property: Proteus's minimiser is the live consumer (it supplies its own order and predicate and asks Hypothesis to run this); the standalone form (c07) already composes it with value-specific move generators.
questions.human_prior: That smaller-first is the right search discipline (never accept a lateral or upward move). The specimen's own initial_coarse_reduction admits the prior costs something: 'they have much more ability to make the test case worse' is why rerandomising moves are quarantined outside the greedy loop.
questions.control: Positive: with predicate always-true and order <, Integer.shrink(1000, ...) returns 0. Negative: with predicate always-false the result equals the start (nothing adopted). Cheat: a version that adopts a non-smaller candidate must be caught by asserting the order strictly decreased on every adoption.
questions.cheat: Reporting a candidate that never satisfied the predicate as the result (unsound minimisation); Techne's receipt measures exactly this as n_unsound (0 of 45) and Proteus's still_solves re-check is the control.
